title: Elon Musk posts ‘Dot.com’ on X as it now redirects to Grok Bot: Is he trolling OpenAI’s new Dots AI...
source_used: Moneycontrol (full text from the fulltext folder); TechJuice (1 Oct 2026) and The American Bazaar (2 Oct 2026) read for dates and background
key_facts: Moneycontrol says a visit to dot.com now redirects to the Grok Bot page, an apparent jab at OpenAI's new Dots AI agents.

Musk highlighted it on X with a short post reading 'Dot.com' while sharing a post from investor and programmer Paul Graham about OpenAI's choice of the name Dots; the date of Musk's post is not given.
OpenAI unveiled Dots at its developer event as AI agents that carry out tasks on their own cloud-based computers; TechJuice dates the launch to Tuesday 29 Sep 2026 at DevDay in San Francisco.

According to 'the report' Moneycontrol cites (not named), the dot.com domain was transferred to xAI in July, well before Dots was announced, so the redirect was not necessarily a response; TechJuice puts the transfer at 28 July.
Why xAI acquired the domain is unclear; xAI has not publicly explained it; one possibility is capturing users who type the address while looking for Dots.
Grok Bot was introduced by xAI earlier this year as an AI teammate that works through a cloud computer and workplace tools; Dots work the same way and connect with thousands of apps.
Background: Musk and OpenAI have a long-running dispute that includes legal cases and rival AI products.
TechJuice (1 Oct) and The American Bazaar (2 Oct) had already covered the redirect, and The Tech Buzz's headline dates the first coverage to 29 Sep 2026.
quote_evidence: Musk highlighted the move on X with a short post reading “Dot.com”, while sharing a post from investor and programmer Paul Graham.
According to the information shared in the report, the dot.com domain was transferred to xAI in July, well before OpenAI announced Dots.
This means the redirect was not necessarily set up in response to OpenAI’s launch.
why_it_matters_hint: A public jab between two rival AI-agent makers; the domain moved to xAI in July, before Dots was announced, and xAI has not explained it, so intent is unproven.
event_date: Redirect and Dots launch from 29 Sep 2026; Musk's 'Dot.com' post is undated in the report; Moneycontrol published on 5 Oct 2026
notes: Reply story: Musk's one-word post names no one, so it is described as 'widely read as' a dig at OpenAI, never stated as fact; Moneycontrol itself notes the redirect was not necessarily a response. Moneycontrol relies on 'the report' without naming it, so the entry credits 'Moneycontrol, citing an unnamed report'. The story began on 29 Sep 2026 (Tech Buzz headline), was covered on 1 and 2 Oct (TechJuice, The American Bazaar) and re-run on 5 Oct (Moneycontrol, Economic Times, NewsBytes), so it is marked as a follow-up of 29 Sep 2026 and the score is lowered by 1. The date of Musk's own post could not be established; if it was posted on 3 or 4 Oct, an editor may keep the item. Detail differs between outlets (xAI is called SpaceXAI by TechJuice; Moneycontrol and The American Bazaar describe Graham's post differently); only agreed facts are used.
